note: Adjudicated variants: 6 accidental (punctuation, capitalization, capital-accents, accents). Substantive text agrees across both witnesses with zero further divergence.

adjudicated.ruling: No comma between the two genitives, with do and with the corpus ruling at ordinarium.memento-vivorum w003.

No comma before the relative clause, with handmissal-eo. In the missal the comma follows the name slot N. et N., which this edition does not print: without the names the clause describes the servants and handmaids themselves and is not parenthetical.

Accented, with do and with the same hand missal's own tuárum in the Meménto of the living: a word of three syllables carries its stress mark (ORTHOGRAPHY.md). The two editions each drop this accent once, in opposite prayers.
Comma after the participle, with handmissal-eo and with the typical edition: it closes the long dative phrase before the accusative locum that the verb governs.
No comma before the et closing the three genitives, with handmissal-eo and with the corpus rulings at ordinarium.confiteor w028 and ordinarium.orate-fratres w021.
No comma before the apposition Dóminum nostrum, with handmissal-eo and with the corpus ruling at ordinarium.aufer-a-nobis w018.
